q: I want to brighten the face of someone who walks across the frame, but my circle stays put and they walk out of it.
a: 1. Park on a frame where the person is clearly visible and add a Circle window on a new node (Windows tab ▸ Circle, `masks.add` on the node) around the face; soften it. 2. Click Track forward in the Windows tab (runs `masks.track`): the window gets a keyframe per frame. 3. Track backward from the same frame for the part before it. 4. Raise Gamma / Gain a little inside the window. 5. Scrub through: where the track slips, move the window back on that frame and track again from there.

q: face window tracking keeps sliding off onto the wall
a: The tracker follows the detail inside the window: a soft window over a flat area loses track. Make the window a bit tighter on the face (eyes, hairline give texture), track again from the last good frame (the new keyframes replace the old ones), and fix the few frames where it still slips by hand.

q: In Premiere I'd use a tracked Lumetri mask to lift a moving subject. What's the Revolution way, and does a planar tracker exist?
a: A window on a grade node does the job of Premiere's Lumetri mask: add an ellipse window (Windows tab ▸ Circle) and click Track forward / backward (`masks.track` with the node). The tracker is a point tracker (Position, Position + Rotation, or Position + Scale + Rotation via `masks.set` `trackMethod`); there is no planar or 3D tracker yet, so on a subject that turns a lot, track in shorter pieces and fix slips by hand.

q: The client wants to choose between a warm look and a cool look. How do I keep both and show them?
a: Revolution has no grade versions yet, so use the Gallery: 1. Grade the warm look and Grab Still (`stills.grab`); rename it with `stills.label`. 2. Change the grade to the cool look and grab a second still. 3. Click a still's thumbnail to compare it with the current frame (Wipe or Split, `compare.set`). 4. When the client picks, select the clips and double-click that still (`stills.apply`) to give them its grade.

q: local grade versions like resolve? want A/B of two grades on the same shot
a: Not yet: there are no Local / Remote grade versions. Keep each alternative as a still in the Gallery (`stills.grab`), compare with Wipe or Split against the live frame (`compare.set`), and apply the chosen one with `stills.apply`.

q: Show three looks for a whole sequence so the director can choose before I grade every shot.
a: 1. Grade one representative shot three ways, grabbing a still of each (`stills.grab`, named with `stills.label`). 2. Compare them in Split against the frame (`compare.set`) with the director. 3. Apply the chosen still's grade to the other clips (`stills.apply`), then adjust each shot for balance; windows copied with a grade keep their position, so re-place or re-track them on other shots. Or duplicate the sequence once per look (`edit.duplicate` on the sequence in the Project panel) if the director wants to watch each one played through.

q: How can I keep my drone and city B-roll shots organised so I can reuse them in every vlog?
a: 1. Keep a folder structure on disk with clear names (by place, by type: drone, city, nature) and import from it in each project. 2. In the project, label B-roll with a fixed label colour (`edit.label.*`) so Select Label Group finds them all. 3. Make a Search Bin (`file.newSearchBin`) whose rule matches a name or label, e.g. every item named 'drone': it fills itself as you import.

q: cant find that sunset shot i used last month in hundreds of clips
a: Search the project panel by name, or make a Search Bin (`file.newSearchBin`) with a rule on the name (e.g. 'sunset') so every match shows in one bin. For next time: clear file names on disk and a label colour per kind of shot.

q: Does Revolution have smart bins like Resolve for a B-roll library?
a: Yes: Search Bins (`file.newSearchBin`) are smart bins: they show every item matching their rules and update as items are added; edit or delete them with `project.editSearchBin` / `project.deleteSearchBin`. A Bin from Selection (`file.newBinFromSelection`) makes an ordinary bin from what you picked.

q: Clouds kept coming and going during my outdoor shoot and every set-up has a different colour. I shot a grey card each time; how do I use it?
a: 1. On the grey card's frame of each set-up, use the white-balance picker (`grade.wb.pick`) on the card. 2. Copy that node to the set-up's other clips (`grade.copy`, `grade.paste`). 3. Then match exposure shot to shot by eye on the scopes. Next time record a few seconds of the card at each new light or camera setting, in the subject's light.

q: Can Revolution match a colour checker chart automatically?
a: Not yet: automatic chart matching isn't offered. Use the chart's grey patch (or a grey card) with the white-balance picker (`grade.wb.pick`), then copy the node to the clips of that set-up (`grade.copy` / `grade.paste`).

q: white balance eyedropper on a grey card premiere style?
a: In Lumetri Color, Basic Correction ▸ WB Selector (`lumetri.wb.pick`): click it, then click or drag on the grey card in the Program monitor. In the node grader the same job is `grade.wb.pick`.
